PCA of Surface Energy Fluxes and Ice Thickness

Data

Each observation is one lake in one month of one year. The variables are the monthly means of each surface flux type (W m⁻²) and the monthly mean ice thickness (m). Only ice-covered hours are used, and months with fewer than 10 ice-covered days are dropped. That leaves 505 observations across 6 lakes.

Every variable is centred and scaled to unit variance before the PCA. Without that, the large radiative fluxes and the metre-scale thickness would dominate just because of their units.

How the variables relate

PCA results

Variance explained

PC1 explains 36% of the variance and PC2 explains 26%. Together the first two components capture 62%, and the first three capture 80%.

Loadings

  • PC1 (36%): high scores mean high Net LW and low Ice thickness, Latent heat. Lakes with the highest mean score: The Loch, Green Lake 4; lowest: Lake Fryxell, Lake Hoare.
  • PC2 (26%): high scores mean high Sensible heat, Latent heat and low Absorbed SW. Lakes with the highest mean score: Lake Fryxell, East Lake Bonney; lowest: Green Lake 4, The Loch.
  • PC3 (18%): high scores mean low Conductive (−Qc), Absorbed SW. Lakes with the highest mean score: The Loch, Green Lake 4; lowest: Lake Fryxell, East Lake Bonney.

The descriptions above list variables with |loading| ≥ 0.35.

Notes

  • The results depend on the model version. The fluxes come from the saved model outputs, so the PCA reflects whatever version of functions.R produced them (shown in the “Output last written” column above). The turbulent fluxes in particular will change once the surface-temperature fix is in.
  • Thickness separates the regions. Perennial Dry Valley ice is roughly 3–5 m thick and seasonal Rockies ice is under about 1 m, so thickness alone pulls the two regions apart. To see how flux patterns differ apart from thickness, remove thickness from pca_vars.
  • Monthly observations are not independent. Months within a lake are autocorrelated, so the PCA is for describing and comparing lakes, not for significance tests.
